methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Foundation of Identity
content: Problem: Students at the beginning of the program lack the basic structures to introduce themselves confidently.

Solution: Week 1 establishes the absolute foundation. We focus on the "be" verb (am / is / are) and basic identity nouns/adjectives so students can construct simple, accurate sentences about who they are.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "Hello World!"
content: Welcome to the Hero Academy! My name is Max. I am a boy. I am 8 years old.
I am a student. I am happy!
This is Luna. She is a girl. She is 9 years old. She is nice.
We are friends. We are students at the Hero Academy. We are happy!

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "We Are Students!"
content: Welcome to the Hero Academy! My name is Max. I am a boy. I am 8 years old.
I am a student. I am happy!
This is Luna. She is a girl. She is 9 years old. She is nice.
We are friends. We are students at the Hero Academy. We are happy!
We are in the classroom. I am a student (học sinh).
Luna is a student, too. She is a smart girl (con gái).
We like to read books. We like to draw pictures.
"Are you happy (vui vẻ) today?" asks the teacher.
"Yes, we are very happy!" we say.
School is a great place to be a student!
T / F: They are in the park.
T / F: Luna is a smart girl.
Fill-in from text: Yes, we are very _________________! we say.
Stage 3B — Inference: Why is school a great place?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "Nice Friends"
content: Welcome to the Hero Academy! My name is Max. I am a boy. I am 8 years old.
I am a student. I am happy!
This is Luna. She is a girl. She is 9 years old. She is nice.
We are friends. We are students at the Hero Academy. We are happy!
I have a friend (bạn bè) named Pip. Pip is a squirrel!
Pip is very nice (tốt bụng). He shares his food with me.
"You are a good friend," I tell Pip.
At school, all the students are nice. We help each other.
It is very important to be nice. Nice friends make us happy!
T / F: Pip is a dog.
T / F: Pip is very nice.
Fill-in from text: We are _________________ friends, says Pip.
Stage 3B — Inference: Why is it important to be nice to your friends?

parts.title: PART 2: VOCABULARY BUILDING — Mastery Level: ALL 8 story words + ALL 3 Cambridge words
PART 3: SENTENCE BUILDING (DIVERSE EXERCISES)
content: Grammar Focus: Bringing it all together (S+V+O & Adjectives)
Review: I am... He is... We are...
Adding Adjectives: She is a nice friend. We are happy students.
Pip là một người bạn tốt bụng.
Bạn là một người bạn tốt.
Mọi học sinh đều tốt bụng.
Những người bạn tốt làm chúng tôi vui vẻ.
Tôi rất vui vì bạn là bạn của tôi.
Cô ấy giúp đỡ bạn bè của mình.
Anh ấy là một cậu bé tốt bụng.
Tên của người bạn của tôi là Luna.
Lớp học của chúng tôi thì tuyệt vời!
[O] L2 — Older: Unscramble the sentence (10 items)
glad / I / you / my / friend. / are / am
Student A: "Are you a nice friend?"
Student B: "Yes, I am a nice friend! I share my food!"
[O] L3 — Older: Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
Pip is a _______________ friend. (nice / rock / car)
You _______________ a good boy. (are / is / am)
Nice friends make us _______________. (happy / sad / scary)
It is _______________ to be nice. (important / bad / sleepy)
Base: Pip is a friend. + Add: (nice)
Base: You are a friend. + Add: (good)
Base: The students are nice. + Add: (all)
Base: Friends make us happy. + Add: (Nice)
Base: She helps her friends. + Add: (always)
Base: He is a boy. + Add: (nice)
Base: My friend's name is Luna. + Add: (best)
Base: Our class is great! + Add: (very)
Base: I am a student. + Add: (happy)

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W1: name, age, boy, girl, student
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (name, age, boy, girl, student) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Simple sentence S+V+O, am / is / are (be verb)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Simple sentence S+V+O, am / is / are (be verb).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Introductions & Identity — Hello World!"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Introductions & Identity — Hello World!".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (name, age, boy, girl, student usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.
